{"title": "[Tropobeat] Ducting reference", "type": "markdown", "aggs": [], "params": {"fontSize": 10, "openLinksInNewTab": false, "markdown": "#### Ducting state (heat-map colour)

| Lvl | State | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Normal (teal) | No point super-refractive or ducting |
| 1 | Super-refractive (yellow) | Bends more than normal; distant stations can come in stronger |
| 2 | Ducting (orange) | A ducting layer, but no duct thick enough to trap the channel |
| 3 | Trapping (rose) | A duct thick enough to trap the channel |

A path takes its **strongest** point, so one point is enough to raise it.

#### Gradient classes

A location is classed by its steepest layer.

| dN/dh (N/km) | Class | Score |
|---|---|---|
| above −79 | Normal | 0 |
| −79 to −157 | Super-refractive | 0 to 0.6 |
| −157 to −300 | Ducting | 0.6 to 1.0 |
| below −300 | Strong ducting | 1.0 |

Standard atmosphere is about −40 N/km.

#### Path index

The mean of the LRF, midpoint and transmitter scores. **Above 0.6** means ducting at one or more points.

#### Trapping

A duct traps a channel only if it is thick enough:
f min (MHz) = 360,000 / thickness^1.5

| Band | Thinnest duct that traps |
|---|---|
| Low VHF (RF 2–6) | 262 to 342 m |
| High VHF (RF 7–13) | 142 to 161 m |
| UHF (RF 14–36) | 71 to 83 m |

*Initial thresholds, not yet calibrated against real events.*
"}}
